name: Check Point — Web C2 Beacon (Recurring Uncommon-Domain Callbacks) [host/user-scoped]
xql_query:
dataset = check_point_application_control_raw
| filter act = "Accept"
| filter cs5Label = "Matched Category" and cs5 = "Uncategorized"
| filter src != null and suser != null and dhost != null
| comp count() as beacon_count by suser, src, dhost, shost
| filter beacon_count >= 8
| alter user_name = suser, int_host = src, url = dhost, host_name = shost
description: Repeated Accepted outbound Application-Control connections from one internal host/user through the Check Point gateway to a single Uncategorized-category domain — the perimeter-firewall signature of an HTTP C2 beacon. Deliberately HOST/USER-SCOPED: it carries suser (the exact box user, resolved by Identity Awareness) and the internal client IP as alert entities so XSIAM attributes the alert to the same asset/user the Cortex endpoint alerts are keyed on, letting endpoint + network fold into one case. Reads the Application Control dataset (check_point_application_control_raw) where the Matched Category / user attribution live.
alert_name: Check Point — Web C2 Beacon (Recurring Uncommon-Domain Callbacks)
alert_description:
What fired: >=8 Accepted Application-Control connections from one internal host/user through the Check Point gateway to a single Uncategorized-category domain within the search window — a low-and-slow HTTP C2 beacon to uncommon infrastructure.

Why it matters: a host is beaconing to rare/uncategorized web infrastructure at a regular cadence (classic C2 check-in). Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (TA0011 - Command and Control).

Investigate:
  - Identify the internal client (host_name/int_host) and user (user_name) and the beaconed domain (url); check domain reputation, registration age, and resolution history.
  - Pivot to the endpoint on the same host/user for the process that opened the connection (correlate with Cortex agent alerts on that asset).
  - Confirm the destination is not an expected/authorized service before escalating.
